record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How many words of a given length are strongly k-abelian nth powers?

evidence.quote: How many words of a given length are strongly k- abelian nth powers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2, and a finite alphabet Σ. Two finite words u, v ∈ Σ* are said to be k-abelian equivalent, written u ∼_k v, if for every word w with |w| ≤ k, the number of occurrences of w as a factor of u equals the number of occurrences of w as a factor of v. A finite word x ∈ Σ* is called a strongly k-abelian nth power if there exist words y_1, y_2, …, y_n with x = y_1 y_2 ⋯ y_n and y_1 ∼_k y_2 ∼_k ⋯ ∼_k y_n.

Determine, as a function of the length N (and of k, n, and |Σ|), the number of words x ∈ Σ^N that are strongly k-abelian nth powers.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results confirm that strongly k-abelian nth powers are an active topic in combinatorics on words (e.g., results on their unavoidability for all k, n), but no source giving an exact enumeration formula or asymptotic count for the number of length-N words that are strongly k-abelian nth powers was found. The status of the counting question appears unresolved in the literature accessible online.

status_evidence.title: Strongly k-Abelian Repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly k-abelian nth powers are not avoidable on any alphabet for any numbers k and n.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational paper introducing strongly k-abelian nth powers and addressing avoidability, but not enumeration of length-N occurrences.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Combinatorics on Words: a Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian combinatorics on words, including k-abelian equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey covers k-abelian topics; no closed-form count for strongly k-abelian nth powers is reported.
